summary: feat(core): script surfaces compose in the deployment document — `agent.ScriptBindings/chain` (core/graph/resource) takes the optional `base` dep first and then every `unit` dep in sorted key order (`base` < `unit` < `unit.*`), the late phase following the same order, so a combination like standard + tokens + audit no longer exists only in host code as an intermediate resource per combination: the engine still takes one provider under `script_bindings`, a host impl binds its own globals only, and a chain replaces the standard fallback like any other provider — mount `standard` as `base` to extend that surface — while the pre-chain pattern keeps working and a chain accepts such a provider as a unit. Attribution is why the merge knows its parts: `bindings.Part` pairs a provider with the owner label the merge reports it under and `Merge` runs both phases over the parts, so a unit whose Bind/BindLate fails is reported with its dep key and keeps its own error classification, a duplicate global names the deps that bound it (global "board" bound by both dep "base" and dep "unit.tokens" — both across units and late against the ordinary phase, the late side alone where the ordinary phase was already merged, since a merge cannot name an owner it never saw), and an empty or unusable global name is reported as that rather than as a duplicate, through the same bindingNameError Assemble applies; `bindings.Chain` is now Merge without owners, refuses a name bound twice itself with Assemble's wording instead of leaving it to Assemble, and the chain resource's own copy of the two-phase logic and its parity test are gone; a provider mounted under two keys is refused at build time (Conflict) where reflection can identify the value, i.e. for pointer-backed providers — `standard`, `chain` and `none` expose no identity under it, so a doubly mounted core impl deploys and is caught by the duplicate-name check at execution time naming both dep keys — and a chain that composes nothing is a build error naming both dep kinds and pointing at `impl: none`, which stays the explicit empty surface; `chain` takes no settings, so an unknown key fails the build instead of being ignored. feat(core/memory): give the resident profile block its own kind and class — ContextProfile is the item kind and ContextSourceProfile the class (the address carries the conversation), naming a block that is not retrieved because a query resembled it but rides along with every request up to its own bound, so a host that wants to read it, weight it, or keep a slot retrieved classes cannot spend has a name for it. feat(core/event): report dropped envelopes instead of losing them silently — the in-process bus reported a buffer-full drop through a branch guarded on an observer that NewMemoryBus always installs as noop (so it was unreachable, and core ships no Observer implementation), leaving Dropped() the only signal and nothing polls it; the bus now reports its own drops whether or not an observer is attached, through a drops.total counter labelled by drop reason and a rate-limited (one per bus per 30s) log line carrying the subject, the per-reason split and the running total, with real loss (buffer full, closed subscription) at Warn while a voluntary Sample-policy rejection stays on the Debug path so a sampling stream does not become a warning generator, and the DropOldest eviction branch that bumped the tally but recorded no drop now does both so the observer, the counter and the log agree; summarizeDropReasons sizes off the enum instead of a hard-coded [3]int, so a new reason is counted rather than silently dropped, the drops.total description no longer claims a per-subscription split the counter does not carry, and the log throttle stores a time.Time instead of wall-clock unix nanos so an NTP step backwards cannot silence drop logging until wall time catches up. fix(core): refuse YAML mappings whose distinct keys collapse onto one JSON key — utils.ToJSON converts YAML through sigs.k8s.io/yaml, which spells mapping keys while iterating a Go map (int and int64 decimal, float64 `g` at float32 precision, bool "true"/"false", the infinities and NaN ".inf"/"-.inf"/".nan"), so `1` beside `"1"`, `true` beside `"true"`, `1` beside `1.0`, `010` beside `"8"`, `.inf` beside `".inf"` and the float32 edges (`1e6` is "1e+06", `16777217.0` is "1.6777216e+07") spelled one JSON key twice and the surviving value was decided by map iteration order — measured at 353 against 47 over 400 runs — so the document is now refused by key rather than by value (a pair collapsing onto two equal values is refused as well, because the JSON holds one key twice and leaves the choice to whichever library reads it next), the walk reuses the tree the single-document check already decoded and runs after the strict decode, and the refusal names the keys in the document's own syntax, sorted, so the message is a function of the document rather than of iteration order (`YAML keys !!int 1, !!str "1" convert to the same JSON key "1"`); over the repository's own corpus nothing changes behavior, and the class is covered by dedicated conformance fixtures. fix(core): report YAML keys the JSON conversion cannot spell — the same conversion names the first key it cannot spell while iterating a map, so a document holding two reported a different one per process (measured on `~` against `18446744073709551615`: 362 against 38 over 400 runs) and the null key's wording even carried `%!s(<nil>)`; utils.UnusableKeys names those keys — `null`, and integers past int64 that still fit in uint64, since a key yaml.v2 cannot hash fails the decode itself with `invalid map key` and an integer past uint64 resolves to a float, which the conversion spells lossily rather than refusing — in one sorted sentence, `YAML keys !!int 18446744073709551615, !!null null cannot be spelled as JSON keys`, and ToJSON refuses such a document after naming every one of them itself, so the refusal is a function of the document like the conversion it stands in for, and a document that fails the strict decode for another reason keeps that failure unless it also holds an unspellable key, which is named first. fix(core): warn about collapsing SKILL.md frontmatter keys — core/skill decodes frontmatter leniently (extension fields accepted, a name that mismatches its directory a warning), so a collapse cannot change what that parser reads (name, description and metadata.short-description are only ever spelled by string keys equal to those names) and the skill keeps loading while the collapse is reported as a warning naming the collision, once per collision in the sorted order of the JSON key, with a collapse under metadata keeping short-description and warning the same way, while a key the conversion cannot spell refuses the file before the lenient decode, named and sorted by the same rules as utils.ToJSON, so neither finding can leak map iteration order; a key written in the two spellings yaml.v2 folds into one stays a silent last-wins tolerance, because the parser's contract accepts shape issues with a warning. fix(core/resource): bound and expire the secret lookup cache — CachingSecretStore held one map entry per name ever resolved, with no capacity and no removal: the TTL only decided when an entry was overwritten on the next lookup of the same name, so a deployment that resolves names as data (one per tenant, request or file key) kept every value and every negative result in memory for the process lifetime, a deployment-level TTL being configurable while the size was not; the cache now holds at most defaultSecretCacheCapacity (256) entries, evicting the entry closest to expiry first, and reclaims expired entries on the same name's next lookup and otherwise in one sweep per TTL window, so a name nobody resolves again is retained for at most one extra window, negative results stay cached at a now-bounded cost, and the bound is configurable through resource.WithCacheCapacity and deploy.WithSecretCacheCapacity; Secret gains GoString, and the store and its entries gain String and GoString that print a redaction marker, so %v, %+v, %s and %#v no longer print every resolved secret. fix(core/utils/httpkit): honor a Retry-After hint up to its own ceiling — a hint clamped by MaxDelay (2s in DefaultRetry) turned a real 429 into a retry storm: the server asked for a minute, the transport slept two seconds, burned the remaining attempts and reported failure while the provider was still rate limiting; RetryConfig gains MaxHintDelay (30s in DefaultRetry), a hint is honored up to that wider ceiling because the server is naming the rate it will enforce but stays bounded so a hostile or misconfigured hint cannot park the caller for hours, a zero or negative MaxHintDelay falls back to MaxDelay, and MaxDelay <= 0 still means no sleep on the exponential path, hints included. fix(core/runtime): read the live generation atomically — Runtime.Resource resolved r.current with a plain field read while Reload assigned the new generation under lifecycleMu, so a reader on another goroutine raced the swap (go test -race reports Reload's write against Resource's read, the practical outcome being a stale or torn generation) although the field comment already promised an atomic swap; current becomes an atomic.Pointer[Generation], Reload and Close store through it, Resource and the lifecycle readers load it without taking the lifecycle lock, the builder's nil checks move to the Store, and TestRuntimeResourceConcurrentReload hammers Resource while reloading under the race detector. fix(core/sandbox/bwrap): keep the env allow-list out of the host argv — the backend rendered the child environment as --clearenv plus one --setenv NAME VALUE pair per allowed variable, and those arguments are part of the host-side argv, so every variable the policy kept — provider API keys included, since the zero-value EnvPolicy keeps the whole host environment — was readable in /proc/<pid>/cmdline by any local process for as long as the exec ran; buildFlags no longer carries env flags at all and childEnv renders the same policy (allow-list, then Inject with override semantics, now sorted for a stable result) as the environment of the bwrap process, which bwrap passes on to the sandboxed command, so the set of variables the child sees is unchanged (PWD aside, which bwrap sets itself), Extra flags still reject --setenv/--clearenv, and the bridge keeps shaping the proxy variables on top of the filtered env. fix(core/utils/net): pin the dial target to an address the net rules cover — the enforcement proxy resolved a hostname locally whenever IP/CIDR rules existed but then dialed the first address of the answer whatever the rules said, so an address the rule set never covered was dialed as long as some other address was allowed or a hostname allow rule had matched, and a rebind or a reordered answer reached a destination the checks never validated; decide now evaluates every answer and pins the dial target to the first address an allow rule actually covers, a deny match anywhere in the answer still denies outright, and when no rule covers any address (deny-only rule sets, or an answer outside the allowed ranges) the hostname rule or the mode default decides and the first address is pinned, so the dial never re-resolves into an unchecked address; the address pass moves into decideAddrs so the ordering rules are testable without a resolver, and an address-only allow now reports the rule that covered it instead of an empty one.
